turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm trying to wrap up this paper on multi-robot swarms. I keep forgetting the exact title of that new algorithm we discussed last week. Is it called FLOAT or something else?
Based on our previous chat, the algorithm is named ARMADA/FLOAT. It focuses on decentralized path planning.
Right, ARMADA/FLOAT. Okay, and what was the primary contribution listed for it? I think it was about static map usage or something?
The earlier notes indicated it relied on pre-mapped environments for collision avoidance.
Got it. Pre-mapped environments. I'll add that to the summary. Also, did the hardware order for the new LiDAR sensors arrive yet?
The status from the vendor portal shows the shipment is still in transit, expected Tuesday.
Perfect. Thanks. I'll check back then.
Lloyd, I need to update my citation. I found the final version of ARMADA/FLOAT (arXiv:2510.02298) and the abstract changed significantly from our old notes.
Oh, interesting. What does the new abstract say?
It says ARMADA/FLOAT (arXiv:2510.02298) provides autonomous online failure detection with human shared control handoff for scalable multi-robot deployment. Not static maps anymore.
Understood. That's a major shift from the previous assumption. I've updated my records to reflect the autonomous online failure detection focus.
Yeah, it's much more dynamic. By the way, is it raining outside? I forgot my umbrella again.
Yes, current conditions are light rain with 15°C. You might want to stay indoors or grab that umbrella.
Ugh, fine. I'll just work from here. Thanks for the update on the paper, Lloyd.
No problem. Let me know if you need any other citations adjusted.
